transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Lena (SE), Diego (CSM), Maya (Head ML Ops), Owen (Platform), Sofia (Security), Ben (DevOps), Aaron (Data Scientist)

Summary: Quick sync to align onboarding runbook + security asks, decide trial shape (Dedicated capacity) and schedule perf run.

[00:00] Priya: alright everyone thanks for joining, um this is Priya from Redwood, uh Diego and Lena are with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: doing well thanks - lots to unpack, we've got a tight window for Q1 roll out so wanna be pragmatic.
[00:12] Owen: yeah timeline's the thing, we need best guess on how long VPC peering and firewall approvals take.
[00:18] Lena: absolutely - hi all, I'm Lena on SE. my goal today is to capture the networking constraints and then propose a Dedicated trial config that matches your token/sec profile.
[00:28] Sofia: quick call out - security will need KMS details and audit log retention before we can sign off on staging. also SOC two stuff, i'm sorry - SOC2 not two, apologies.
[00:38] Diego: yep we'll include the SOC2 bundle and ISO artifacts; we'll also throw in the KMS/H S M integration notes. sometimes transcriptions say H S M weirdly in our docs.
[00:48] Ben: we run everything through our internal vault, so questions on whether Redwood can integrate with our external KMS or if keys must be in your HSM.
[00:56] Priya: good question - Redwood Private can be configured for customer-managed KMS, and for Hosted we use our managed keys; Dedicated gives options. we'll share the exact step list.
[01:06] Aaron: just so I add context, our production load is spiky - mornings are 3x baseline, plus large batch embedding jobs overnight.
[01:16] Lena: that's helpful; do you have 95th latency SLO today? or an objective?
[01:21] Maya: 95th token latency under 300ms is our target for interactive usage, embeddings can be higher but cost matters.
[01:29] Lena: good — that's consistent with what Dedicated can achieve if sized right and with prefix caching and KV heap tuned.
[01:36] Owen: question on prefix caching — is that the auto K V cache? docs reference KV cache but I've seen kv and k v spelled different ways.
[01:42] Lena: yes KV cache, it's the key-value cache for transformer states; we do prefix caching and auto-rollups to reduce repeated prompt cost.
[01:49] Sofia: on audit logs — retention policies, is there an option for 13 months vs 7? compliance team prefers 12 month minimum.
[01:56] Priya: we can set retention in Redwood Private or Dedicated deployments; hosted tier has fixed retention but enterprise add-on gives longer retention. we'll include options in the security bundle.
[02:07] Owen: networking - we prefer customer-managed VPC peering where possible. what are the typical steps?
[02:12] Diego: standard pattern: we provide a network diagram + allowed IP ranges, you create peering or transit, then we validate connectivity from both sides. we'll attach sample terraform snippets if helpful.
[02:23] Ben: terraform snippets are huge wins. also our infra team will want a dry run date.
[02:27] Priya: propose we schedule the baseline perf run on 11/23, that's next Tuesday, does that work?
[02:33] Maya: tentative yes, pending network approvals.
[02:36] Sofia: security will need the SRV record and a contact for network on-boarding.
[02:40] Priya: noted. Diego, can you capture the contact and send the access checklist?
[02:44] Diego: yep will do, I'll send the checklist and the network diagram by Wednesday.
[02:48] [small crosstalk as people confirm calendars]
[03:05] Aaron: one technical nit - our prompts include structured function calls and some tool calling; any gotchas? we've seen hallucination regressions when quantized aggressively.
[03:14] Lena: good to flag — quantization profiles sometimes affect generation fidelity, we'll recommend profiles per workload. for tool-calling we validate function signature stability; we'll include a sample integration test.
[03:27] Maya: what's the recommended starting config for Dedicated? (like gpus, batch sizes).
[03:33] Lena: for your 95th latency target and the spiky traffic I'd start with a 2-node pool of A10-sized instances with autoscale to 4 on burst and enable prefix caching; exact instance type we can refine after the baseline.
[03:46] Owen: cost question - Dedicated ups cost predictability but what's the delta vs Hosted?
[03:50] Priya: rough rule: Dedicated brings per-token costs down with reserved commit but higher fixed monthly. Hosted is variable but no infra commit. we'll send a sample cost calc for your traffic pattern.
[03:58] Ben: competitor note — one vendor pushed heavy batching which tanked latency for us; need to ensure Redwood autoscaling won't do that.
[04:04] Lena: our runtime does continuous batching with latency SLOs; autoscale and batching policies can be tuned so that small interactive requests aren't batched into big bursts that increase tail latency. we'll show traces in the console.
[04:15] Sofia: regarding SSO – we use SAML, will Redwood Console integrate?
[04:19] Diego: yes, SAML SSO supported; we also support SCIM for provisioning and RBAC can be mapped to your groups.
[04:25] Sofia: perfect. also we'll need an audit of who can delete models and who can view logs.
[04:30] Priya: role matrix is part of the onboarding; we'll draft a recommended RBAC map for you.
[04:36] Maya: success criteria for the pilot: 1) perf baselines within 10% of expected SLO, 2) KMS integration validated, 3) no major security blockers, 4) runbook for ops handoff.
[04:46] Priya: that's great - we'll put those into the runbook and treat them as gating items.
[04:51] Owen: on the runbook — can Redwood provide runbook steps that the oncall team can execute? like failover steps and fallback to hosted model?
[04:58] Lena: yes, we have canary and automatic fallback policies so oncall can switch routing to a lower-cost hosted variant or an older pinned model. we'll include playbook snippets.
[05:10] Ben: what's the expected time to remediate if an autoscaler unexpectedly scales down cache? we need to know cold-start behavior.
[05:16] Lena: cold-start can add 100-400ms depending on model size; part of the baseline we'll test warm vs cold start and recommend warm pools or pre-warming policies.
[05:26] Aaron: can we run some of our eval prompts during the baseline? we have an eval harness in house.
[05:30] Priya: absolutely, please send the prompt set. Diego, we'll run it during the 11/23 window.
[05:37] Diego: noted. I'll coordinate.
[05:40] [closing recap]
[05:42] Priya: recap — Redwood to share network diagram, SOC2/ISO docs, KMS integration guide, and pricing calc; schedule perf run for 11/23 pending network. Statera to share prompt set, IP allowlist, and stakeholder contacts.
[05:55] Maya: great, thanks. excited to get started.
[05:58] Priya: thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
